web.description: A how-to guide for Stimulus: tones, sweeps with hold and scrub, harmonics, noise with band limiting and burst, the Stereo ID and GLITS channel idents, polarity pops, analyzer-matched measurement signals, mixing four generators, and exporting test files.
web.ogDescription: What each generator does and how to use it: tone, sweep, harmonics, noise, Identify, Measure, the rack, master section and export.

cta.title: Stimulus
cta.text: A four-generator test signal rack for live sound: tones, sweeps, harmonics, noise, stereo idents and polarity pops, plus period-matched measurement signals.
cta.buyNote: App Store · one purchase covers Mac and iPad

intro.text: Stimulus generates test signals for PA tuning and audio work: steady tones, sweeps you can hold and scrub, harmonic stacks, three noise colours with band limiting, identification tones (GLITS and polarity Pop), and measurement excitation for a transfer-function analyzer. Up to four generators run at once through a small mixer with a safety limiter on the output.

blocks.text: The editor shows one generator at a time; the rack on the right holds them all. Click a strip to edit it, press **+ Add generator** to spawn another (up to four), hold a strip - or right-click it on a Mac - to remove it, and drag a strip to reorder the rack. Each strip has its own level fader plus **M** (mute), **S** (solo) and the polarity flip. The reset control by the generator label defaults the current mode's own settings without touching the mix.
Each generator can be a different type - run a tone against a sweep, or two tones for dual-tone tests. The transport at the bottom right starts and stops everything together.

Type a frequency or use the slider, which runs the full 10 Hz to 22 kHz range, always clamped to what your output device can actually reproduce. The row of recall keys under the field jumps straight to 60 Hz, 100 Hz, 400 Hz, 1 kHz or 10 kHz, and the slider follows.

Null and cancellation tests: two tones at the same frequency with one polarity flipped cancel exactly when their phases are aligned. Phases align at Play, so set your frequencies first and then press **Play**. If you move a frequency while running, that generator's phase drifts relative to the others (the price of click-free frequency glides) - tap **Play** again to restart from the top and re-align.

Set the range by typing **Start** and **End** or by dragging the two thumbs on the range slider - the ringed thumb is the end. Crossing the thumbs (or the swap button) gives a down sweep. Sweeps run log or linear over the set duration.

items: **Return** sweeps to the end frequency and back to the start, with a seamless turnaround.
**Loop** repeats the sweep until you stop it.
**CONT/STEP** switches to stepped mode: the sweep dwells on each 1/3-octave frequency for the set dwell time, including the end frequency.

blocks.text: While a sweep runs, **HOLD** freezes it at the frequency on screen and keeps it sounding as a steady tone. A bright thumb appears on the range slider - drag it (or use the arrow keys) to move the held tone anywhere in the sweep range. Hold again resumes the sweep from wherever you left it.
**Play** always restarts from the top, even out of hold - tap it repeatedly to retrigger a sweep.

A fundamental with subharmonics below it and harmonics above: f/4, f/3, f/2, the fundamental, then 2f to 5f, each on its own fader. The label under each fader shows the actual frequency it lands on; a dash means that partial falls outside the playable range and stays silent. Everything is phase-locked to the fundamental. Each partial adds its own level on top of the fundamental, so the combined level is higher than a plain tone at the same setting. The master limiter still caps the output at -3 dBFS.

Three colours, ordered by slope: **Red/Brown** (-6 dB per octave), **Pink** (-3) and **White** (flat). Pink is the usual choice for PA work; red/brown is the same signal Smaart calls red. White is flat per hertz, the reference for FFT work.
**Band limit** restricts any colour to one octave or 1/3 octave around a centre frequency - set the centre with the frequency controls that appear. Band-limited pink on a sub is the classic use.

**Burst** gates the noise on and off instead of running it continuously: set how long each burst lasts and how often it repeats. Useful for exciting an analyzer without filling the room with continuous noise, and for hearing a room's decay between bursts.

Four by-ear checks for what is plugged where, whether it is in polarity, and whether it is in time. Two of them identify a stereo pair: both are 1 kHz on both channels, both always feed both channels, and both want the level at -18 dBFS for the EBU reference.

items: **Stereo ID** is the EBU ident: the left channel drops out for 250 ms every 3 seconds and the right runs continuously, so the channel with the gap is left. Summed to mono it is a phase check too - a correct pair dips 6 dB through the gap, while a polarity-reversed pair cancels to silence and the gap becomes a short pip instead.
**GLITS** drops the left once each cycle and the right twice. One break is left, two is right, so each channel is explicitly identified rather than inferred from the other.

blocks.text: **Pop** is a positive-going pulse at a set interval for polarity checks. **HF** is a short 0.5 ms pulse for tweeters and HF sections; **FULL** is the standard 4 ms pulse; **SUB** stretches it to 20 ms so it reads through subwoofers. The first movement is always positive - if your tester or ears say otherwise, something in the chain is flipped.

**Click** is a sharp broadband click for aligning delays by ear. Send it to two outputs - mains and delays, or delays and fills - and listen where they meet. In sync it is one click; out of sync it smears or doubles.
Both the Pop and the Click sit on the same rate clock, so either can be sped up or slowed down while it runs without the transient in flight being cut short.

Measurement excitation for a transfer-function analyzer such as Smaart. Choose a signal and an FFT frame size - 32K, 64K or 128K - to match your analyzer. Each signal is built to be periodic at that frame and looped, so the analyzer averages it to high coherence without spectral leakage. Signal and frame size lock while playing; stop to change them.

items: **Pink** - periodic pink noise for transfer function and RTA, equal energy per octave.
**Sweep** - a cycle-synchronised log sweep, 20 Hz to 20 kHz, for impulse response and transfer function.

blocks.text: Export writes exactly one frame at the output device's sample rate, with no end fades and an embedded loop point, so the file loops seamlessly in your analyzer. The sample rate is shown in the sidebar - keep it matched to whatever is capturing the measurement.

Each generator has a level fader, fade in/out times, and an **Output** switch: left channel, right channel, or both (dual mono - no centre dip). The keys beside the fader recall -6, -12 and -18 dBFS in one tap. The master section has its own fader, always-visible meters, and a safety limiter, on by default at -3 dBFS, that hard-clips rather than letting four summed generators overshoot. Below the ceiling it does nothing at all - it is a safety clamp, not a compressor - and the LIM key glows bright while it is actually clamping.

**DIM** ducks the output 20 dB so you can talk over the system - tap it again, grab the master fader or type a level to restore. Behind the master strip's three-dot button are master fade in/out times and an auto-stop timer that ends playback after a set duration; with **Repeat** on it cycles play and stop until you stop it.
New generators always start at -18 dBFS. Nothing in Stimulus ever defaults to full scale.
Stimulus reopens as you left it: every generator, the mix and the master section are saved when you stop playback or quit, and restored at launch.

Export renders the current setup to a WAV or AIFF file - 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz at 16, 24 or 32-bit float - for any length you set, named after what it contains. Files start and end with a 10 ms fade so they never click, and renders are deterministic: the same setup produces the same file every time. A Measure generator instead exports exactly one FFT frame at the device sample rate, with no fades and an embedded loop point, so it runs on repeat in an analyzer.

items: **Return** - play, or restart from the top while running
**Left/Right arrows** - nudge the frequency (or scrub a held sweep) by 1%; add **Shift** for 10%
